q: Which sequence correctly describes the lifecycle of a secure baseline?
opts: Maintain, then baseline after a breach
Establish once and inherit it for all future systems
exp: SY0-701 defines baseline activities as establish, deploy, and maintain. Deploying before defining produces inconsistency, waiting for a breach is reactive, and freezing a baseline forever leaves it obsolete as vulnerabilities and requirements evolve.
tip: Maintenance is the step organizations skip. A baseline that is never updated becomes a documented list of outdated settings.

q: Which action is part of hardening a network switch?
opts: Configure all ports as trunk ports for flexibility
Leave the default SNMP community strings for compatibility
exp: Disabling unused ports and services and confining management to a protected VLAN reduce attack surface. Telnet transmits credentials in cleartext, universal trunking invites VLAN hopping, and default SNMP community strings are publicly known.
tip: Switch hardening: disable unused ports, set ports to access mode explicitly, change default credentials, use SSH and SNMPv3, and enable port security.

q: Before deploying access points in a new warehouse, engineers walk the facility measuring signal strength and interference, producing a coverage map. What are these activities called?
opts: A site survey producing a heat map
exp: Site surveys measure real-world RF conditions and produce heat maps that guide access point placement, channel selection, and power settings. The other activities assess vulnerabilities, simulate attacks, or exercise plans rather than map coverage.
tip: Site survey deliverables: heat map, channel plan, AP placement, and identification of interference sources and rogue APs.

q: Which improvement does WPA3-Personal provide over WPA2-Personal?
opts: It reduces the key length to improve performance on IoT devices
It disables management frame protection to improve compatibility
exp: WPA3 uses SAE (Dragonfly), so capturing the handshake does not permit offline password cracking, and it also mandates protected management frames. A passphrase is still used, key strength increased rather than decreased, and management frame protection is required rather than disabled.
tip: WPA3-Enterprise adds 192-bit security suites; WPA3-Personal's headline feature is SAE replacing the WPA2 4-way handshake weakness.

q: A company must authenticate each wireless user individually with centralized policy and per-user session keys. Which configuration is required?
opts: WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X and a RADIUS server
WPA3-Personal with a strong shared passphrase
Open authentication with a captive portal terms page
MAC address filtering with a hidden SSID
exp: Enterprise mode with 802.1X and RADIUS authenticates each identity separately and derives unique keys per session. A shared passphrase cannot distinguish users, an open network with a terms page provides no authentication, and MAC filtering with SSID hiding is trivially defeated.
tip: Hidden SSIDs and MAC filtering are not security controls on this exam — they appear as attractive wrong answers.

q: Which capability is central to a mobile device management platform in a BYOD environment?
opts: A managed work profile with selective wipe
Full device wipe as the only option
exp: In BYOD, containerization with a managed work profile lets the organization enforce controls and wipe corporate data selectively while leaving personal content untouched. Full-device wipe without consent, blanket app bans, and OS replacement are impractical or legally problematic for personally owned devices.
tip: Deployment models: BYOD (user-owned), COPE (corporate-owned, personally enabled), CYOD (choose your own device from an approved list).

q: An organization purchases devices, retains ownership and full management rights, and permits limited personal use. Which deployment model is this?
exp: Corporate-owned, personally enabled devices are company property under full management with permitted personal use. BYOD devices are user-owned, CYOD lets users select from an approved corporate-purchased list, and air-gapped provisioning is not a mobile deployment model.
tip: Control ranks COPE > CYOD > BYOD; privacy concerns rank inversely.

q: Which practice is the MOST fundamental defense against injection vulnerabilities in a web application?
opts: Renaming database tables to odd values
exp: Validation and encoding must occur server-side because clients are fully controlled by the attacker. Client-side checks improve usability but are bypassed with a proxy, and obfuscation or naming tricks are security through obscurity.
tip: Never trust client-side controls. Any validation that matters must be enforced on the server.

q: Which cookie attribute combination BEST protects a session identifier?
exp: Secure restricts the cookie to HTTPS, HttpOnly prevents script access to limit XSS impact, and SameSite mitigates cross-site request forgery. The remaining attributes control scope and lifetime rather than security posture.
tip: Session security also requires regenerating the identifier at login and invalidating it server-side at logout.

q: A security team wants to find vulnerabilities in source code before compilation, during each pull request. Which technique should be used?
exp: SAST analyzes source or bytecode without execution and integrates naturally into code review pipelines. DAST tests a running application, fuzzing production risks outages, and post-release penetration testing finds issues far later and at higher cost.
tip: SAST = white box, no execution, early. DAST = black box, running app, later. Both find different defect classes.

q: Why should an organization require code signing for internally developed applications distributed to endpoints?
opts: Signing obfuscates the application against reverse engineering
Signing satisfies supply chain dependency scanning requirements
exp: Code signatures provide authenticity and integrity verification at execution time. Signing does not improve performance, does not encrypt the binary, and does not identify vulnerabilities in the code.
tip: Protect signing keys in an HSM. A stolen code-signing key lets an attacker publish trusted malware.

q: An email gateway opens attachments in an isolated instrumented environment to observe behavior before delivery. Which technique is this?
exp: Sandboxing executes untrusted content in isolation to observe malicious behavior without risking production. Hashing verifies integrity, tokenization substitutes sensitive values, and load balancing distributes traffic.
tip: Evasive malware may detect sandboxes and stay dormant, so sandboxing complements rather than replaces endpoint detection.

q: Why is a complete and accurate asset inventory considered foundational to security operations?
opts: It replaces the need for vulnerability scanning
It satisfies all regulatory requirements by itself
exp: Unknown assets are unpatched, unmonitored, and unprotected by definition, which is why inventory underpins every other control. Inventory may inform purchasing but does not primarily reduce cost, does not replace scanning, and does not by itself achieve compliance.
tip: Asset management steps: acquisition/procurement, assignment and ownership, classification, tracking/enumeration, and disposal.

q: A company must dispose of SSDs that contained regulated data and requires documented assurance the data is unrecoverable. Which approach is BEST?
opts: A single-pass file deletion and emptying the recycle bin
Reformatting the drives with a quick format
Degaussing the SSDs with a magnetic field
exp: SSD wear leveling makes overwrite-based methods unreliable, so cryptographic erase or validated sanitization plus destruction is used, with certification for audit evidence. Deletion and quick formats leave data recoverable, and degaussing works on magnetic media but not on flash.
tip: Sanitization ladder: clear (overwrite), purge (crypto erase, secure erase), destroy (shred, incinerate). Match to data sensitivity and get certificates.

q: Which step is REQUIRED when decommissioning a server that held sensitive data, in addition to sanitizing storage?
opts: Retain its firewall rules for later
exp: Decommissioning must remove the system's identities, trust artifacts, and network references so orphaned credentials and stale rules cannot be abused. Retaining DNS entries, enabled accounts, and firewall rules creates exploitable remnants.
tip: Stale DNS records enable subdomain takeover; orphaned service accounts and firewall rules are recurring audit findings.

q: Legal requires that email for employees involved in pending litigation be preserved, while the standard retention policy deletes email after two years. What must happen?
opts: A legal hold must suspend routine deletion for the affected accounts
The retention policy must be applied uniformly regardless of litigation
All email older than two years must be deleted immediately for consistency
The affected employees should archive messages to personal storage
exp: A legal hold overrides normal retention and deletion for relevant data; failing to honor it risks spoliation sanctions. Uniform deletion, accelerated deletion, and personal archiving all jeopardize evidence integrity and defensibility.
tip: Legal hold suspends destruction. E-discovery is the process of identifying, collecting, and producing that data.

q: Which security activity belongs in the acquisition and procurement phase of asset management?
opts: Assigning the device to a departing employee
exp: Security requirements must be evaluated before purchase, including supportability, patch cadence, and end-of-life dates, because these decisions constrain the asset's entire lifecycle. Sanitization and disposal certification occur at end of life.
tip: Ask at purchase time: how long is it supported, how are patches delivered, and can it meet our baseline?

q: What is the difference between a CVE identifier and a CVSS score?
opts: CVE rates severity; CVSS assigns the identifier
CVE measures exploitability while CVSS lists affected products
exp: CVE is the catalog identifier for a known vulnerability, while CVSS is the scoring framework expressing severity from base, temporal, and environmental metrics. Neither is vendor-proprietary in the way described, and the roles in the wrong answers are reversed.
tip: CVSS base score alone is not risk. Combine it with exploitability in the wild, exposure, and asset criticality.

q: A scanner reports a critical vulnerability on a server, but manual verification shows the affected component is not installed. What is this finding, and what should be done?
opts: A false positive; document and tune
A false negative; increase the scan frequency
An exception; accept the risk permanently without documentation
exp: A reported vulnerability that does not actually exist is a false positive; the correct handling is documented verification, justified suppression, and scanner tuning to reduce noise. A false negative is a missed real vulnerability, and undocumented permanent acceptance is poor governance.
tip: False positive = alarm with no fire. False negative = fire with no alarm, and it is the more dangerous of the two.

q: Which engagement type gives testers no prior knowledge of the environment, simulating an external attacker's perspective?
exp: Unknown-environment testing withholds internal details so the tester must perform discovery like an outsider. Known-environment testing provides full documentation and access, partially known testing provides limited information, and a configuration review inspects settings without adversarial simulation.
tip: Also know the rules of engagement: scope, timing, allowed techniques, escalation contacts, and written authorization.

q: A company publishes a policy inviting external researchers to report vulnerabilities safely and offers rewards for valid findings. What is this called?
exp: Responsible disclosure programs, often paired with bug bounties, provide legal safe harbor and incentives for external reporting. Penetration tests and red team exercises are scoped, contracted engagements, and scans are automated assessments.
tip: Bug bounty benefits: continuous, diverse testing at scale. Requirement: a clear scope, safe harbor language, and a triage process.

q: Which threat intelligence source is BEST described as freely available information gathered from public sources such as vendor advisories, blogs, and social media?
exp: OSINT is publicly available intelligence. Proprietary feeds are paid and curated, dark web monitoring targets criminal marketplaces and forums, and SIEM telemetry is internally generated data.
tip: Also know information-sharing organizations (ISACs) — sector-specific communities that exchange threat data among members.

q: Two vulnerabilities both score CVSS 9.8. One affects an internet-facing payment API; the other affects an isolated lab workstation with no sensitive data. What determines remediation order?
opts: The alphabetical order of the CVE identifiers
The age of the affected hardware
Whichever system the scanner listed first
exp: Identical base scores are differentiated by environmental context: exposure, data sensitivity, and business impact. Arbitrary ordering criteria have no bearing on risk.
tip: CVSS environmental metrics exist precisely to adjust base scores for your environment — use them or apply equivalent business context.

q: In risk analysis, what does exposure factor represent?
opts: The share of asset value lost
exp: Exposure factor is the proportional loss to an asset from a realized threat, used with asset value to compute single loss expectancy. Occurrence frequency is the annualized rate of occurrence, and control cost is a separate input to cost-benefit analysis.
tip: SLE = asset value × exposure factor. ALE = SLE × ARO. Expect at least one calculation-style question.

q: After patching 200 servers, what is the appropriate way to confirm the vulnerabilities are actually resolved?
exp: Rescanning independently validates remediation, catching patches that failed to apply, required a pending reboot, or were rolled back. Deployment status, delayed audits, and verbal confirmation are weaker evidence.
tip: Validation methods on SY0-701: rescanning, audit, and verification. Reporting closes the loop.

q: A business-critical application cannot be patched for six months due to vendor incompatibility. What is the correct governance step?
opts: Silently mark the finding as a false positive
Delete the finding from the vulnerability management system
Disable scanning of the affected host
exp: Legitimate delays are handled through documented exceptions with compensating controls, an expiry date, and accountable approval. Mislabeling, deleting findings, and excluding hosts from scans conceal risk rather than manage it.
tip: Every exception needs four things: justification, compensating controls, an owner, and an expiration date.

q: A development team must be alerted when any third-party library in their application has a newly published vulnerability. Which capability provides this?
opts: Endpoint antivirus scanning of the build server
exp: Software composition analysis inventories dependencies and continuously matches them against vulnerability databases. Network signatures, periodic penetration tests, and antivirus scanning do not track library versions in the codebase.
tip: SBOM (software bill of materials) plus continuous package monitoring is the expected answer for dependency risk.

q: Which activity BEST describes a system or process audit in vulnerability management?
opts: An automated scan for missing patches
An attempt to exploit a discovered weakness
A vendor's marketing assessment of product features
exp: Audits independently verify design and operating effectiveness of controls and processes. Scanning identifies technical findings, exploitation is penetration testing, and vendor assessments are not independent verification.
tip: Internal audit reports to management or the board; external audit provides third-party assurance to customers and regulators.

q: Which action MOST improves the security baseline of a cloud account?
opts: Keep access keys in the repository
exp: Identity hardening, elimination of standing privilege, and comprehensive logging address the most common cloud compromise paths. Shared accounts destroy attribution, unrestricted regions expand exposure and complicate residency, and keys in repositories leak constantly.
tip: Cloud baseline essentials: MFA everywhere, no root/owner daily use, least-privilege roles, logging enabled in every region, and posture monitoring.

q: Which change reduces the attack surface of a newly deployed Linux web server?
opts: Allow root password login over SSH
Give the web account sudo rights
exp: Removing unneeded software, blocking direct root login, and using keys eliminates common exploitation and brute-force paths. Root password SSH, unnecessary desktop packages, and privileged service accounts all increase risk.
tip: Linux hardening extras: SELinux or AppArmor enforcing, host firewall, minimal listening services, and separate non-privileged service accounts.

q: Which combination BEST hardens corporate workstations against common malware delivery?
opts: No local admin, block macros, EDR
exp: Privilege reduction, macro controls, behavioral detection, and timely patching address the dominant infection chains. Duplicate antivirus products conflict, disabling updates and firewalls removes protection, and granting admin rights amplifies malware impact.
tip: Standard user rights alone break a large share of malware and most privilege-dependent persistence techniques.

q: Which hardening approach is MOST appropriate for ICS devices that cannot run security agents and tolerate no unplanned downtime?
opts: Segment and monitor at the network
Put controllers on the user VLAN
exp: When host-based controls are impossible, protection shifts to the network with segmentation, tight flow control, and passive monitoring, plus patching coordinated with the vendor and process schedule. Agent installation and automatic updates risk instability, and flat placement with user systems increases exposure.
tip: For OT, remember the Purdue model concept: layered zones with controlled conduits between IT and OT.

q: A credentialed vulnerability scan finds significantly more issues than an uncredentialed scan of the same hosts. Why?
opts: They inspect from inside the host
exp: Credentialed scans read the actual system state, producing more complete and accurate results with fewer false positives. Uncredentialed scans see only exposed services, which limits both depth and accuracy regardless of platform.
tip: Credentialed scanning is more accurate but requires protected scan accounts — a common exam consideration for least privilege.

q: Two similar companies apply different remediation deadlines to the same vulnerability severity. Which concept explains this difference?
opts: Differing organizational risk tolerance and appetite
Differing CVE identifiers for the same flaw
exp: Risk tolerance reflects how much risk an organization is willing to carry, which shapes remediation SLAs and exception policies. Base scores and CVE identifiers are standardized, and scanner licensing does not set deadlines.
tip: Risk appetite is the strategic willingness to take risk; risk tolerance is the acceptable variance around it in practice.

q: Which configuration change hardens an edge router?
opts: Enable ICMP redirects and directed broadcasts for troubleshooting
Allow SNMP v1 from any source for monitoring
Turn off logging to conserve CPU
exp: Reducing services, filtering spoofed source addresses, and authenticating routing updates prevent common network-layer attacks. Redirects and directed broadcasts enable abuse, SNMPv1 from anywhere exposes device data, and disabling logging removes detection capability.
tip: Anti-spoofing (BCP 38) on ingress prevents your network from sourcing forged traffic used in reflected DDoS attacks.

q: Why does asset management require an assigned owner for each system?
opts: An accountable owner makes risk decisions
Owners physically maintain the hardware themselves
Ownership assigns the classification level automatically
exp: Assigned ownership creates accountability for risk acceptance, access approval, and lifecycle management, without which systems become orphaned. Depreciation is a financial matter, physical maintenance belongs to operations, and classification remains necessary.
tip: Orphaned assets are the most likely to be unpatched and forgotten — a recurring theme in breach case studies.

q: Which response option is appropriate when a vulnerability cannot be patched and compensating controls cannot fully mitigate the risk, but the system is required for operations?
opts: Ignore the finding until the next scan cycle
Remove the system from the asset inventory
Hand it to the help desk
exp: Residual risk that cannot be remediated or mitigated must be accepted through documented governance at an authority level matching the impact. Ignoring findings, removing inventory entries, and reassigning to an unrelated team are avoidance behaviors, not risk management.
tip: Four responses to risk: mitigate, transfer, avoid, accept. Insurance is transfer; segmentation is mitigation.

q: Which monitoring approach BEST detects unauthorized configuration changes on critical servers?
opts: Weekly review of disk space utilization
exp: File integrity monitoring detects unauthorized modification of critical files and is often required by compliance frameworks. Capacity metrics, surveys, and license reports do not detect tampering.
tip: FIM generates noise during legitimate patching, so integrate it with change management to correlate approved changes.

q: Which metric is MOST useful in a vulnerability management report to executives?
opts: Mean time to remediate critical findings
The total number of scan jobs executed
The size in gigabytes of the scan result database
The number of scanner plugins updated
exp: Executives need outcome metrics tied to risk exposure and accountability, such as remediation speed and overdue high-risk items. Operational activity counts and storage statistics do not describe risk reduction.
tip: Report trends and time-to-remediate, not raw finding counts — counts fluctuate with scan coverage and tell leadership little.

q: Which mobile connection method poses the greatest risk of an on-path attack against corporate data in a public setting?
opts: Bluetooth paired to a known headset
exp: Open or attacker-controlled Wi-Fi allows interception and evil twin attacks when traffic is not tunneled. Cellular with a VPN is well protected, restricted Bluetooth pairing has a very short range and limited exposure, and NFC requires proximity and uses tokenized values.
tip: Mobile policy essentials: always-on VPN, certificate-based Wi-Fi, disable auto-join to open networks, and restrict Bluetooth discoverability.

q: A security team compares DHCP leases, switch MAC tables, endpoint agent check-ins, and cloud inventories to find devices missing from the CMDB. What is this activity called?
exp: Enumeration discovers and reconciles actual devices against recorded inventory, exposing unmanaged assets. Penetration testing simulates attacks, classification labels data, and change review evaluates proposed modifications.
tip: Multiple discovery sources beat one: agents miss unmanaged hosts, and network discovery misses powered-off or cloud-only assets.

q: Which input validation strategy is MOST secure for a field that should contain only a five-digit ZIP code?
opts: Deny-list validation blocking known SQL keywords
Trimming whitespace and truncating to 20 characters
exp: Allow-list (positive) validation defines exactly what is acceptable and rejects all other input, which is far more robust than trying to enumerate bad patterns. Deny lists miss encodings and novel payloads, truncation does not constrain content, and escaping alone is not validation.
tip: Prefer allow-list validation with strict types, lengths, formats, and ranges — and always enforce it server-side.

q: How should indicators of compromise from a threat feed be operationalized MOST effectively?
opts: Email the list to all staff weekly
Keep them in an annual spreadsheet
exp: Automated ingestion with context and aging keeps detections current, and retrospective hunting reveals past compromise. Emailing users, static spreadsheets, and permanent unmanaged blocklists produce stale indicators and operational breakage.
tip: Indicators expire. Infrastructure gets reassigned, so unmanaged permanent blocks eventually break legitimate services.

q: A configuration scan shows that 30 of 500 servers deviate from the approved baseline. What is the MOST appropriate response?
opts: Update the baseline to match the 30 servers so the report is clean
Exclude those servers from future scans
exp: Deviations must be triaged into approved exceptions versus unauthorized drift, then corrected with enforcement improved to prevent recurrence. Rewriting the baseline to match drift defeats its purpose, exclusions hide risk, and mass rebuilds are disproportionate.
tip: Configuration drift is inevitable without enforcement. The exam favors automated remediation over repeated manual cleanup.

q: A tester submits malformed and random inputs to a running API to discover crashes and unexpected behavior. Which technique is being used?
opts: Fuzzing as part of dynamic analysis
exp: Fuzzing sends malformed or random input to a running target to uncover input-handling flaws, which is a dynamic technique. Static analysis and code review inspect code without execution, and composition analysis examines dependency versions.
tip: Fuzzing finds crashes and memory-safety bugs that code review often misses; run it in a non-production environment.

q: A third-party vendor shreds decommissioned drives. What should the organization obtain and retain as evidence?
opts: A verbal confirmation from the driver
A photo of the truck departing
exp: Documented certificates with asset identifiers create an auditable chain of accountability for media destruction. Verbal confirmation, incidental photos, and marketing material are not evidence of specific asset destruction.
tip: Chain of custody applies to disposal too: track media from removal to destruction with signatures at each handoff.

q: A hardening baseline for web servers should require which of the following?
opts: HTTP available alongside HTTPS with no redirect
exp: Modern TLS with strong suites plus HSTS prevents downgrade and cleartext exposure. SSLv3 is broken, unredirected HTTP invites interception, and directory listing discloses site structure.
tip: HSTS forces browsers to use HTTPS for a defined period, mitigating SSL-stripping attacks.

q: Which classification distinguishes a vulnerability that requires local access from one exploitable across the network?
opts: The attack vector metric within CVSS
exp: CVSS attack vector (network, adjacent, local, physical) expresses how the vulnerability can be reached, materially affecting priority. Publication year, support tier, and depreciation are irrelevant to exploitability.
tip: Other CVSS base metrics to know: attack complexity, privileges required, user interaction, and the CIA impact subscores.

q: Which control is MOST practical for hardening embedded medical devices that receive vendor firmware updates twice a year?
opts: Isolate, monitor, and patch on vendor cadence
Install a full endpoint protection suite on each device
Grant clinical staff administrative access for faster troubleshooting
exp: Segmentation, tight flow control, passive monitoring, and disciplined vendor patching fit devices that cannot host security software or accept arbitrary updates. Agents may be unsupported or void certification, arbitrary update sources add supply chain risk, and broad admin access increases exposure.
tip: Medical and industrial devices are often certified for a specific configuration — unauthorized changes can void certification or safety approval.

q: Which THREE elements are essential to a functioning vulnerability management program?
exp: Coverage, prioritization with deadlines, and verified closure form the operational core of vulnerability management. A zero-vulnerability policy is unachievable and drives concealment rather than remediation.
tip: Program maturity signals: full asset coverage, authenticated scans, SLAs by severity and exposure, verified closure, and trend reporting.
